description: The exposure category an instrument is shown under. The category the user chose (exposureKind) always wins, with source user. With none chosen it is derived from Instrument.type, with source derived: STOCK is COMPANY, CRYPTO is CRYPTO (a stablecoin included), COMMODITY is COMMODITY. Any other type, ETF, BOND and CASH, has no category, kind null and source none: a fund's type does not say what it holds. exposureLeafId, where a case carries it, is ignored without a category: it never makes the category the user's. The derived category is computed at read and never stored or synced. Shared with the mobile client: both implementations must reproduce every case. expect is written by running the TypeScript core; byHand.figures, where a case has it, are worked out by hand, its arithmetic says how, and each key is a dotted path into expect.

cases.name: A stock with no category chosen is a company

byHand.arithmetic: A share is one company; the type alone says so.

cases.name: A crypto asset with no category chosen is crypto
A stablecoin is crypto too: nothing stored tells it apart

byHand.arithmetic: Kraken's subclass stable_coin is read from the row and not stored, so the instrument is a CRYPTO like any other.

cases.name: A commodity with no category chosen is a commodity
A fund with no category chosen stays unclassified

byHand.arithmetic: Trade Republic sends equity funds, bond funds and gold ETCs alike as ETF, so the type decides nothing.

cases.name: A bond with no category chosen stays unclassified
Cash with no category chosen stays unclassified
A leaf id left without a category changes nothing

byHand.arithmetic: Only a category the user chose is the user's; a leaf id stored beside no category is not a choice, so the type decides.

cases.name: A fund the user classified keeps that category
A gold ETC the user classified as a commodity

byHand.arithmetic: The user's category is taken as it is.

cases.name: The user's category wins over the one the type would give

byHand.arithmetic: A stock derives COMPANY, but a category chosen by the user always decides.
